title.narrative: Provision of communications services in Monguno, Banki, and Dikwa

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to restore and stabilize critical communications services in the humanitarian hubs of Monguno, Banki, and Dikwa, where recent service disruptions have severely impacted operational coordination and staff safety. These disruptions, caused by the premature depletion of prepaid internet services and disconnections by Internet Service Providers (ISPs), threaten to disconnect over 1,600 humanitarian personnel from more than 100 UN and NGO organizations working in Northeast Nigeria. The Emergency Telecommunications Sector (ETS), led by the World Food Programme (WFP), is currently underfunded and has not yet received donor commitments, making it increasingly difficult to sustain services. Despite these financial constraints, ETS plans to implement strategic solutions to keep prepaid services active, settle outstanding ISP obligations, and reinforce communications infrastructure in the affected locations.ltbrgtThe communications services provided by ETS are essential enablers of humanitarian action, supporting secure communication, real-time coordination, and access to critical information that allows responders to deliver timely and effective assistance while they remain safe. By ensuring uninterrupted communications, the project will strengthen collaboration among humanitarian actors, safeguard personnel operating in high-risk areas, and support the delivery of life-saving services to vulnerable populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
